checks.name: Exactly 50 MIDI files with matching IDs across files and both CSVs
Every MIDI file parses with mido
Tempo and 4/4 time-signature meta at tick 0, 480 PPQ, 1/2/4-bar loops
checks.detail: tempo compared within 0.01 BPM after microsecond rounding

checks.name: End-of-track at the loop boundary; every note-on has a note-off; no same-pitch collisions
checks.detail: note-on/off pairing done independently from the generator

checks.name: Pitches 24-64 (C1-E4), velocities 1-127, positive durations, notes inside the loop
Monophonic; overlaps only in legato-labeled patterns, each at most 1/8 beat, never same pitch
Note-event CSV and index CSV match the parsed MIDI exactly (pitch, tick, duration, velocity, names)
checks.detail: beats cross-checked against ticks; note names converted back to MIDI numbers (MIDI 60 = C4)

checks.name: Every out-of-scale note is labeled as an intentional chromatic departure (recomputed from key + scale)
No exact, transposed, re-velocitied, re-tempoed, or near-duplicate patterns
checks.detail: rhythm+duration twins: 0; identical onset grids: 0 (none); closest onset grids BP13/BP34 Jaccard 0.94; closest onset+pitch-class tokens BP08/BP31 Jaccard 0.50 (fail threshold 0.85)

checks.name: All seven groove families present; loop lengths span 1, 2, and 4 bars
checks.detail: families acid 7, offbeat 7, rolling 8, sparse 7, staccato 7, sustained 6, syncopated 8; bars 1-bar 12, 2-bar 25, 4-bar 13

checks.name: Proxy: every ghost note (velocity < 90) is no longer than the pattern's median normal note
checks.detail: 11 ghost notes checked; this is a proxy, not a listening test

checks.name: ZIP passes CRC test and every member is byte-identical to the validated files

limitations: Musical quality, groove feel, and velocity-insensitive playability are judgments; only the ghost-note proxy is automated.
Glide behavior on legato overlaps depends on the receiving instrument and cannot be verified from MIDI.
DAW import was not tested inside commercial DAWs in this environment; files were parsed with mido and @tonejs/midi.
Near-duplicate detection uses onset and pitch-class set similarity; it cannot judge perceived similarity.

second_parser.detail: PPQ, tempo, 4/4 time signature, end-of-track tick, and every note (pitch, start tick, duration, velocity) compared with the CSVs
